html:
The Constitution of Mongolia, adopted on 13 January 1992, ended seventy years of one-party communist rule and made Mongolia a parliamentary democracy. It came out of the peaceful democratic revolution of 1990, and it renamed the Mongolian People's Republic simply Mongolia.

It set up a parliament of one chamber, the State Great Khural, with 76 members; a directly elected president with a veto; and a Constitutional Court. It guarantees freedom of speech, religion and movement and the right to private property, and it declares the land and its minerals the property of the people, under state protection.

Mongolia became one of the few lasting democracies in the former Soviet sphere in Asia, squeezed between Russia and China, with power changing hands through elections many times. Leaders of 1990 such as Zorig took part in shaping it. An amendment in 2019 strengthened the prime minister and limited the president to a single six-year term, and one in 2023 enlarged the Khural to 126 seats. The national flag still carries the Soyombo symbol.
